# Project Context: Content Hub V2 (Local-First Skill Engine)

## What V2 Is

A **local-first content production engine** that lives at `C:\Users\madhu\Claude cowork\Content Hub V2\`. Modeled on Chase AI's 10M-views workflow. Stops at the script — no automated rendering. Produces **9 deliverables per long-form** via 7 Claude Code slash-commands.

V2 is a **fork** of V1 (the SaaS-stack project at `C:\Users\madhu\Claude cowork\Content Hub\`). V1 is parked. V2 is where all active work happens. Decision logged in [[2026-04-28_V2_Pivot_Local_First_Engine]] (V1 vault).

## Current State — 2026-04-28

**Phase 0 (Cleanup) — not yet started.** V2 currently contains a full clone of V1 and needs SaaS layers stripped before build can begin.

See [[Current_Sprint]] for the live task list.

## Architecture (V2)

Two-layer skill pattern, repeated 7 times:

```
.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md   ← Claude Code entry point (/<name> trigger)
skills/<name>.py                 ← Python helper, calls model(s), writes to vault
prompts/<name>.md                ← Single source of truth for prompt text
```

**Cost-aware model routing:**
- **Ollama (local, free)** — first-draft outlines, structural work
- **Claude (paid)** — hooks, titles, voice cleanup, final-30-second polish
- **Gemini** — kept available for any tool that already wires it (research_service.py)

**Knowledge layer:**
- `notebooklm-py` (already cloned in V2) — programmatic NotebookLM access for one-shot Callaway masterclass extraction + ad-hoc deep research
- `Content-Hub-Vault/` (this vault) — human-facing workspace and skill output target
- pgvector RAG (`backend/research/rag.py`) kept available, deprioritized in v1

- discovery-to-mvp-coach: Guide a user from a vague problem observation to an executable 21-day Manual MVP plan through structured scientific discovery: observation, causal modeling, falsifiable hypothesis, assumption testing, Mom Test interview practice, and synthetic persona stress-testing. Use this whenever someone wants to investigate or validate a problem before building, pressure-test a problem statement or idea, design a low-cost manual experiment to test a thesis, or move from observation to hypothesis to testable MVP, even if they do not name a framework. Use this skill whenever the user types /cascade, says "generate distribution content", "create social posts from my outline", "write a blog post from my research", "turn this into a Twitter thread and LinkedIn", "cascade this", or asks to repurpose a YouTube video into written content for multiple platforms. Generate 5 Kallaway-trained YouTube hook variations for a video topic — the critical first 30 seconds that stop the scroll and open a curiosity loop. Use this skill whenever the user types /hook, asks to "write hooks", "generate hooks", "create my opening", "write my intro", "give me hooks for", or mentions wanting attention-grabbing YouTube video openings. - ideation: Step 2 of 8 in the content production pipeline (/researcher → /ideation → /hook → /outline → /title → /cascade → /short-form → /voice-cleanup). Use this skill whenever the user types /ideation, says "generate ideas", "what video should I make", "give me video ideas", or asks what to do after research. Always trigger after /researcher completes. After showing the 9 ideas, ask the user to pick one before suggesting /hook — this choice determines the entire downstream pipeline.

Use this skill whenever the user types /orchestrate or /delegate, or says "orchestrate this", "dispatch agents", "delegate this", "use multi-agent", or "use the orchestrator". Also trigger automatically when the task spans 3+ subtasks, touches 2+ specialist domains (e.g. schema + backend + frontend, or any combination of roles from AGENTS.md), or involves 10+ files across subsystems. ## COMPREHENSIVE BACKEND & PIPELINE ARCHITECTURE REPORT

### 1. MAIN.PY — API ENDPOINTS & ROUTES

**File:** `c:\Users\madhu\Claude cowork\Content Hub V2\Design-doc\server\main.py`

All routes are FastAPI POST/GET endpoints. CORS allows `http://localhost:5173` only.

#### Health & Vault Routes

```python
@app.get("/api/health")
# Response: { "status": "ok", "backend": "up", "capabilities": null }

@app.get("/api/vault/recent")
# Params: folder (str, default "10-Research"), limit (int, max 50), subfolders_only (bool)
# Response: [{ "name": str, "path": str, "modified": ISO timestamp }]

@app.get("/api/vault/file")
# Params: path (str) — vault-relative or absolute
# Response: { "path": str, "content": str (raw markdown) }

@app.get("/api/vault/outputs")
# Params: path (str)
# Response: [{ "name": str, "path": str }]
```

#### Job Status & Streaming

```python
@app.get("/api/jobs/{job_id}")
# Response: { 
#   "job_id": str,
#   "stage": str (e.g. "researcher", "ideation", "trends"),
#   "status": "running" | "completed" | "failed",
#   "started_at": ISO timestamp,
#   "completed_at": ISO timestamp | null,
#   "result": { "result_type": "file"|"bundle"|"brain_result", 
#               "primary_path": str, "outputs": list[str], "data": dict | null } | null,
#   "error": str | null
# }

@app.get("/api/jobs/{job_id}/stream")
# Returns: Server-Sent Events stream
# Events: { "type": "stdout"|"stderr"|"done"|"error"|"ping", 
#           "line"?: str, "result"?: {...}, "error"?: str }
```

#### Pipeline Stage Endpoints (All POST, all check conflict via `_check_conflict()` which returns 409 if another job running)

```python
@app.post("/api/pipeline/trends")
# Body: TrendsBody { "space": str = "" }
# Returns: { "job_id": str }

@app.post("/api/pipeline/researcher")
# Body: ResearcherBody {
#   "niche": str (required),
#   "repos": list[str] = [],
#   "mode": str = "deep",
#   "trend_repo": str = ""
# }
# Returns: { "job_id": str }

@app.post("/api/pipeline/ideation")
# Body: IdeationBody {
#   "topic": str (required),
#   "research_file": str = "",
#   "no_trends": bool = False
# }
# Returns: { "job_id": str }
```

### 3. HOW THE BACKEND GETS "TRENDS"

**Trends File:** `c:\Users\madhu\Claude cowork\Content Hub V2\scripts\github_trending.py`

**Vault Output:** `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/04-Trends/github_trending.md`

**Mechanism:**
1. `github_trending.py` queries GitHub API for repos created in last 30 days with topics `["llm", "ai", "machine-learning"]`.
2. Splits results into 7-day and 30-day windows client-side (fetches 40, filters).
3. Calls `claude CLI` to pick one repo from each window as video topic candidates.
4. For each shortlisted repo (~15 total), calls `claude CLI` again to generate a "deep dive" markdown file.
5. Writes individual repo breakdowns to `04-Trends/<owner_repo>/<owner_repo>.md`.
6. Renders a master index at `04-Trends/github_trending.md` with tables, Claude's picks, and deep-dive cross-refs.

### 6. STAGE OUTPUTS & FRONTEND DATA FLOW

**Output Return Mechanism: Not Files, Not JSON — Job Results + SSE**

When a stage completes:

1. **Frontend starts the stage:**
   ```javascript
   const { job_id } = await runStage("ideation", {
     topic: "AI agents",
     research_file: "10-Research/2026-05-31_ai-agents_brief.md"
   });
   ```

2. **Job runs in background subprocess, streams events via SSE:**
   ```javascript
   // Opens EventSource to /api/jobs/<job_id>/stream
   // Receives events: { type: "stdout", line: "..." } (one per subprocess line)
   //                  { type: "stderr", line: "..." }
   //                  { type: "done", result: { result_type, primary_path, outputs } }
   //                  { type: "error", error: "..." }
   ```

3. **On completion, JobResult returned:**
   ```json
   {
     "result_type": "file",
     "primary_path": "Content-Hub-Vault-V2/02-Ideas/2026-05-31_ai-agents.md",
     "outputs": ["Content-Hub-Vault-V2/02-Ideas/2026-05-31_ai-agents.md"],
     "data": null
   }
   ```

4. **Frontend then reads the file:**
   ```javascript
   const { content } = await readVaultFile(result.primary_path);
   ```

**Single-Job-at-a-Time Constraint:**
- Global `_current_job_id` tracks the running job (set in `jobs.py`).
- Any new POST to a pipeline endpoint checks `_check_conflict()` → returns 409 if a job is running.
- Cleared on completion or failure.
- **Frontend must warn user if conflict detected and suggest waiting or cancelling.**

**No Job Polling Mechanism — Only SSE:**
- `/api/jobs/{job_id}` is for **status checking only** (returns snapshot of job state).
- `/api/jobs/{job_id}/stream` is the **real-time event pipe** (SSE, no polling).
- Stream drains buffered events first, then waits up to 30s between new events (ping keepalive every 30s).

### 6. STAGE OUTPUTS & FRONTEND DATA FLOW

**Output Return Mechanism: Not Files, Not JSON — Job Results + SSE**

When a stage completes:

1. **Frontend starts the stage:**
   ```javascript
   const { job_id } = await runStage("ideation", {
     topic: "AI agents",
     research_file: "10-Research/2026-05-31_ai-agents_brief.md"
   });
   ```

2. **Job runs in background subprocess, streams events via SSE:**
   ```javascript
   // Opens EventSource to /api/jobs/<job_id>/stream
   // Receives events: { type: "stdout", line: "..." } (one per subprocess line)
   //                  { type: "stderr", line: "..." }
   //                  { type: "done", result: { result_type, primary_path, outputs } }
   //                  { type: "error", error: "..." }
   ```

3. **On completion, JobResult returned:**
   ```json
   {
     "result_type": "file",
     "primary_path": "Content-Hub-Vault-V2/02-Ideas/2026-05-31_ai-agents.md",
     "outputs": ["Content-Hub-Vault-V2/02-Ideas/2026-05-31_ai-agents.md"],
     "data": null
   }
   ```

4. **Frontend then reads the file:**
   ```javascript
   const { content } = await readVaultFile(result.primary_path);
   ```

**Single-Job-at-a-Time Constraint:**
- Global `_current_job_id` tracks the running job (set in `jobs.py`).
- Any new POST to a pipeline endpoint checks `_check_conflict()` → returns 409 if a job is running.
- Cleared on completion or failure.
- **Frontend must warn user if conflict detected and suggest waiting or cancelling.**

**No Job Polling Mechanism — Only SSE:**
- `/api/jobs/{job_id}` is for **status checking only** (returns snapshot of job state).
- `/api/jobs/{job_id}/stream` is the **real-time event pipe** (SSE, no polling).
- Stream drains buffered events first, then waits up to 30s between new events (ping keepalive every 30s).

**File:** `scripts/github_trending.py` + `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/04-Trends/github_trending.md`

**Source of Trends:**
- Runs GitHub API search for repos with topics: `llm`, `ai`, `machine-learning` (line 31)
- Groups results by creation date (last 7 days vs. last 30 days)

- Generates "deep dive" markdown files for each repo

```markdown
→ Deep dive: [[owner_repo/owner_repo]]

```

**Parseable Structure:**
- **Markdown tables** — can be parsed with regex or markdown library for repo list
- **Markdown links** — can extract owner/repo from `[owner/repo](url)` pattern
- **Mark with 🎯** — Claude's picks are highlighted

**For your web page:**
- Read `04-Trends/github_trending.md`
- Extract repos from the table: `[owner/repo](...)`
- Let user pick from the list
- User picks → trigger `/researcher --repos owner/repo1 owner/repo2`

| Skill | Main Entry | Async? | Returns | Writes To |
|-------|-----------|--------|---------|-----------|
| **researcher** | `async def run(niche: str, mode: str, repos: list[str]) -> Path` | Yes | `Path` to brief file | `10-Research/YYYY-MM-DD_*.md` |
| **ideation** | `async def main()` (reads sys.argv via argparse) | Yes | None (writes file internally) | `02-Ideas/YYYY-MM-DD_*.md` |
| **outline** | `async def main()` (reads sys.argv via argparse) | Yes | None (writes file internally) | `06-Outlines/YYYY-MM-DD_*.md` |

---

### 7. VAULT FOLDER STRUCTURE (Reference)

```
Content-Hub-Vault-V2/
├── 00-Management-V2/      # brief.md — governance config
├── 02-Ideas/              # ideation output
├── 04-Trends/             # github_trending.md + deep dives
├── 05-Hooks/              # hook skill output
├── 06-Outlines/           # outline skill output
├── 07-Titles/             # title skill output
├── 08-Distribution/       # cascade skill output
├── 10-Research/           # researcher skill output (main briefs)
└── 09-Shorts/             # short-form skill output
```

---

### 8. WEB PAGE FEATURE RECOMMENDATIONS

Based on this architecture, your web page pipeline should:

1. **Trends → Pick Repo Step:**
   - Parse `04-Trends/github_trending.md` 
   - Show tables + Claude's picks
   - User selects 1–2 repos
   - **Action:** Trigger researcher subprocess

2. **Researcher Completion → Review Research:**
   - Read output from `10-Research/YYYY-MM-DD_*_brief.md`
   - Show repo sections (synthesized brief)
   - **Action:** Auto-advance or user confirms to ideation

3. **Ideation → Pick Idea Step (BLOCKING GATE):**
   - Parse `02-Ideas/YYYY-MM-DD_*.md`
   - Extract all 9 ranked ideas (regex on Rank N headings)
   - Show title + angle + format for each (1–2 lines)
   - **Blocking:** User MUST pick a rank (1–9) before moving forward
   - **Action:** Pass chosen title to hook subprocess

4. **Hook → Review Hooks (Optional Gate):**
   - Show 5 hook variations from `05-Hooks/YYYY-MM-DD_*.md`
   - User picks which hook to use (default: hook #1)
   - **Action:** Pass hook path + topic to outline subprocess

5. **Outline → Review Outline:**
   - Show Dopamine Ladder stages from `06-Outlines/YYYY-MM-DD_*.md`
   - User reviews structure
   - **Next:** Short-form, titles, cascade, etc.

---

All file paths are absolute. All skills are subprocess-callable or async-importable. The ideation output is **structurally parseable** for pick-one-of-9 user selection.

content.text: I now have the full picture. Before finalizing the approach, let me pressure-test it with the advisor — there are a couple of design forks (fresh-scan vs. pick-existing trends, whether to include the hook step, and a fragile markdown-parsing requirement for the "pick an idea" selector).

Your approach is sound — proceed with it. A page-level state machine (trends → research → ideation → outline) with a single `useJobStream`, where selecting an option triggers the next `runStage`, is the right shape. It naturally respects the one-job-at-a-time constraint, and "select = auto-run next" matches what the user asked for. Don't re-architect. A few sharpenings before you write the plan:

**1. Cut the parsing surface to almost nothing.** Your sub-agent proposed parsing ideation into full JSON (angle, gap, audience_desire, …). You don't need any of that — the only field the next stage consumes is the **title** (→ `outline.topic`). So:
- **Ideation:** parse *only* the `### Rank N — Title` headings into a pick-list; render the full prose via `MarkdownViewer` for reading. Title-heading regex is robust; full-field parsing is fragile and unused. (§2 Simplicity.)
- **Trends:** don't parse the `github_trending.md` table at all. `getRecent("04-Trends", subfoldersOnly=true)` already returns one entry per repo deep-dive — that IS your pick-list, and each path is exactly what `trend_repo` wants. You already leaned this way; lock it in.

Keep a real manual-entry fallback for the ideation parse (if <2 headings found, let the user type the topic). Theoretical fallbacks rot.

**2. Your "pick the research" read is correct — say it explicitly in the plan.** Researcher emits **one** brief, so there's nothing to multi-select. That step is a review/approve gate (show brief → "Use this → run ideation"), not a picker. That's the honest handling of a singular artifact — don't manufacture a selection UI where the output is one file.

**3. Each gate needs a `failed` branch.** `useJobStream` surfaces `status:"failed"` + error. If research or ideation fails mid-pipeline, show the error and offer **retry that one stage** — don't dead-end the whole run. Also handle `ConflictError` on the first `runStage` (a job from another view could be live).

**4. Mirror the exact body shapes from StageWorkspace.jsx:234–238.** That resolves the discrepancy between your two sub-agent reports on researcher args — the ground truth is `{ niche, repos: [], mode, trend_repo }` (repos can be empty; `trend_repo` is the deep-dive path, and pipeline.py extracts the GitHub URL from it). Your top-level seed input feeds both `trends.space` and `research.niche`.

**Trim your questions to the two real forks** — drop the nav-naming one (just pick "Pipeline" / "Auto Run" yourself):
- **Trends source:** pick from today's vault trends *(recommended — instant)* vs. run a fresh scan first *(github_trending.py is minutes-long, many Claude calls — bad as a blocking first step)*.
- **Hook step:** honor the user's literal four steps (ideation → outline directly) vs. insert the hook gate. This isn't cosmetic: `outline` takes `topic` (+ optional `hook_path`) and does **not** receive the research brief — so without hook, the chosen idea reaches outline as a bare title with no research context flowing through. The hook gate is where that context would flow in. Worth surfacing so the user chooses knowingly.

No blocker here — these are forks, not problems. Ask the two questions, then write the plan.
Excellent guidance. Let me confirm the two real product forks with you, then I'll write the plan.

"""FastAPI orchestration service — port 8765.

Start from repo root:
    .venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m uvicorn main:app --app-dir Design-doc/server --port 8765 --reload

All skill subprocess invocations use the same repo .venv (see runtime.md).
"""

import asyncio
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel

# Ensure sibling modules (jobs, pipeline, vault, brain) are importable
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))

import brain as brain_module
import jobs
import pipeline
import vault

app = FastAPI()

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["http://localhost:5173"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Health
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {"status": "ok", "backend": "up", "capabilities": None}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vault
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@app.get("/api/vault/recent")
async def vault_recent(folder: str = "10-Research", limit: int = 10, subfolders_only: bool = False):
    return vault.recent(folder, min(limit, 50), subfolders_only)


@app.get("/api/vault/file")
async def vault_file(path: str):
    content = vault.read_file(path)
    if content is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="File not found or path outside vault")
    return {"path": path, "content": content}


@app.get("/api/vault/outputs")
async def vault_outputs(path: str):
    return vault.outputs(path)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Job status + SSE stream
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@app.get("/api/jobs/{job_id}")
async def get_job(job_id: str):
    job = jobs.get_job(job_id)
    if not job:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")
    return {
        "job_id": job.job_id,
        "stage": job.stage,
        "status": job.status,
        "started_at": job.started_at,
        "completed_at": job.completed_at,
        "result": (
            {
                "result_type": job.result.result_type,
                "primary_path": job.result.primary_path,
                "outputs": job.result.outputs,
                "data": job.result.data,
            }
            if job.result
            else None
        ),
        "error": job.error,
    }


@app.get("/api/jobs/{job_id}/stream")
async def stream_job(job_id: str):
    job = jobs.get_job(job_id)
    if not job:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")

    async def _events():
        # Drain already-buffered events (handles race where job finishes before
        # the client connects to the SSE endpoint)
        while not job.queue.empty():
            event = job.queue.get_nowait()
            yield f"data: {json.dumps(event)}\n\n"

        if job.status in ("completed", "failed"):
            return

        while True:
            try:
                event = await asyncio.wait_for(job.queue.get(), timeout=30.0)
                yield f"data: {json.dumps(event)}\n\n"
                if event.get("type") in ("done", "error"):
                    break
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                yield f"data: {json.dumps({'type': 'ping'})}\n\n"

    return StreamingResponse(
        _events(),
        media_type="text/event-stream",
        headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"},
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Conflict guard
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _check_conflict():
    current = jobs.get_current_job_id()
    if current:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=f"Job {current} is already running")

5	  2. Calls launch_job(), which spawns the subprocess and streams stdout/stderr
6	     into the job's asyncio.Queue.
7	  3. On exit-0, calls the stage-specific resolver to produce a typed JobResult.
8	  4. Returns the job_id immediately (non-blocking).
9	
10	Resolvers parse known stdout markers first; deterministic-slug fallbacks are
11	used only when parsing fails. No skill files are modified (§3 Surgical Changes).
12	"""
13	
14	import asyncio

40	def _bundle_result(output_dir: str) -> JobResult:
41	    dir_path = Path(output_dir)
42	    members = sorted([str(p) for p in dir_path.glob("*.md")]) if dir_path.exists() else []
43	    primary = (
44	        str(dir_path / "README.md")
45	        if (dir_path / "README.md").exists()
46	        else (members[0] if members else output_dir)
47	    )
48	    return JobResult(result_type="bundle", primary_path=primary, outputs=members or [output_dir])

1	"""Vault file reader.
2	
3	Exposes three operations used by /api/vault/* endpoints:
4	  - recent(folder, limit)  — newest .md files in a vault subfolder
5	  - read_file(path)        — raw markdown content
6	  - outputs(path)          — list members of a bundle directory or single file
7	
8	All path inputs are validated against VAULT_ROOT before any file access
9	(path-traversal guard).
10	"""
11	
12	from datetime import datetime
13	from pathlib import Path
14	from typing import Optional
15	
16	PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent
17	VAULT_ROOT = (PROJECT_ROOT / "Content-Hub-Vault-V2").resolve()
18	
19	
20	def _safe_resolve(path_str: str) -> Optional[Path]:
21	    """Return resolved Path only if it falls inside VAULT_ROOT, else None."""
22	    try:
23	        p = Path(path_str)
24	        if not p.is_absolute():
25	            p = VAULT_ROOT / p
26	        resolved = p.resolve()
27	        if not str(resolved).startswith(str(VAULT_ROOT)):
28	            return None
29	        return resolved
30	    except Exception:
31	        return None
32	
33	
34	def recent(folder: str, limit: int = 10, subfolders_only: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
35	    """List the most-recently-modified .md files in a vault subfolder.
36	
37	    Searches both direct children and one level of subdirectories so that
38	    researcher outputs written to dated subfolders (e.g. 10-Research/2026-05-06_ruflo/)
39	    appear alongside flat _brief.md files.
40	
41	    subfolders_only: when True, skip top-level .md files and only include files
42	    from one-level-deep subdirectories (used for 04-Trends repo pickers).
43	    """
44	    target = VAULT_ROOT / folder
45	    if not target.exists() or not target.is_dir():
46	        return []
47	    all_md: list[Path] = []
48	    for item in target.iterdir():
49	        if not subfolders_only and item.is_file() and item.suffix == ".md":
50	            all_md.append(item)
51	        elif item.is_dir():
52	            for sub in item.iterdir():
53	                if sub.is_file() and sub.suffix == ".md":
54	                    all_md.append(sub)
55	    files = sorted(all_md, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime, reverse=True)[:limit]
56	    return [
57	        {
58	            "name": f.relative_to(target).as_posix() if f.parent != target else f.name,
59	            "path": str(f),
60	            "modified": datetime.fromtimestamp(f.stat().st_mtime).isoformat(),
61	        }
62	        for f in files
63	    ]
64	
65	
66	def read_file(path_str: str) -> Optional[str]:
67	    """Read a vault file's raw markdown. Returns None if path is unsafe or missing."""
68	    resolved = _safe_resolve(path_str)
69	    if not resolved or not resolved.exists() or not resolved.is_file():
70	        return None
71	    return resolved.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
72	
73	
74	def outputs(path_str: str) -> list[dict]:
75	    """List readable members for a bundle directory or single file."""
76	    resolved = _safe_resolve(path_str)
77	    if not resolved:
78	        return []
79	    if resolved.is_dir():
80	        files = sorted(
81	            [f for f in resolved.iterdir() if f.is_file() and f.suffix == ".md"],
82	            key=lambda p: p.name,
83	        )
84	        return [{"name": f.name, "path": str(f)} for f in files]
85	    if resolved.is_file():
86	        return [{"name": resolved.name, "path": str(resolved)}]
87	    return []
88

input.content:
# Full Pipeline Page — Step-by-Step Human-in-the-Loop Run

## Context

The web app (`Design-doc/web`) today exposes each pipeline stage as an isolated workspace (`StageWorkspace`, `DistributionWorkspace`). There is no way to run the **whole chain end-to-end** while reviewing and selecting at each gate. This adds a new, separate page that walks the user through the entire content pipeline:

**trends → research → ideation → hook → outline → title → cascade → short-form**

At each stage the generated output comes back to the user, they make a selection (or approve), and **the next stage runs automatically** with that selection threaded into its input. This honors the user's request for "an automatic step-by-step full pipeline run menu in which all the prompts come back to the user, and it can just select and make sure the next step loads automatically."

Two product decisions confirmed with the user:
- **Trends source:** default to the instant vault list (`getRecent("04-Trends", …, subfoldersOnly=true)`) **plus a "Refresh trends" button** that runs a fresh scan on demand.
- **Scope:** the full chain through short-form (hook step included).

No backend changes are needed — every stage already has an endpoint, body model, and result resolver. This is a **frontend-only** addition.

## How each stage is consumed (ground truth)

All calls go through `runStage(stage, body)` → `{ job_id }`, then `useJobStream(jobId)` → `{ lines, status, result }`. `result` = `{ result_type, primary_path, outputs, data }`. Body shapes verified in `Design-doc/server/main.py:145-201`; arg threading in `Design-doc/server/pipeline.py`.

| Stage | Gate | Body sent (`runStage`) | What we read from result | What flows forward |
|-------|------|------------------------|--------------------------|--------------------|
| trends | **pick 1** (+refresh) | refresh only: `{ space: seed }` | n/a (pick from vault list) | `trendPath` = picked `.md` path |
| research | **approve** | `{ niche: seed, repos: [], mode: "deep", trend_repo: trendPath }` | `primary_path` → `briefPath` | `briefPath` |
| ideation | **pick 1 of 9** | `{ topic: seed, research_file: briefPath, no_trends: false }` | fetch `primary_path`, parse `### Rank N — Title` | `ideaTitle` (selected heading) |
| hook | **approve** | `{ topic: ideaTitle, platform: "yt-long", audience: "", format: "medium", research_file: briefPath, no_polish: false }` | `primary_path` → `hooksPath` | `hooksPath` |
| outline | **approve** | `{ topic: ideaTitle, hook_path: hooksPath, length: 8, platform: "yt-long", no_polish: false }` | `primary_path` → `outlinePath` | `outlinePath` |
| title | **pick 1** | `{ concept: ideaTitle, outline_file: outlinePath }` | fetch `primary_path`, parse `- **<title>**` | `titleString` (selected) |
| cascade | **approve** | `{ research_file: briefPath, outline_file: outlinePath, title: titleString, youtube_url: "" }` | bundle (`outputs[]`) | — |
| short-form | **terminal** | `{ research_file: briefPath, outline_file: outlinePath, title: titleString, youtube_url: "" }` | bundle (`outputs[]`) | — (done) |

**Why "approve" not "pick" for research / hook / outline / cascade:** each produces a *single* artifact (one brief, one hooks file, one outline, one distribution bundle), and the downstream skill consumes the **whole file path** (`research_file` / `hook_path` / `outline_file`). There is nothing to multi-select, so those gates are a review-and-continue. Only **ideation** and **title** emit a discrete list whose chosen item becomes a *string* input downstream (`ideaTitle` → next topics; `titleString` → cascade/short-form `title`) — those are the true picker gates. (Per advisor: don't manufacture a picker where the output is one file.)

**Trend path correctness:** `recent(subfolders_only=true)` returns each inner `.md` file's full path (`vault.py:55-63`), which is exactly what `pipeline._github_url_from_trend_file` reads to extract the GitHub URL for `--repos`. So passing the picked `path` straight into `trend_repo` works.

## Files to change

### 1. `Design-doc/web/src/FullPipelinePage.jsx` (new)
The page component. A page-level state machine, one `useJobStream`, vertical stepper UI.

State:
```js
const [seed, setSeed] = useState("");            // niche/space — drives trends refresh + research.niche + ideation.topic
const [jobId, setJobId] = useState(null);
const [runningStage, setRunningStage] = useState(null);  // which stage the live job belongs to
const [gate, setGate] = useState("trends");      // current stage awaiting user action
const [picks, setPicks] = useState({ trendPath:null, briefPath:null, ideaTitle:null, hooksPath:null, outlinePath:null, titleString:null });
const [stageError, setStageError] = useState(null);
const jobStream = useJobStream(jobId);
```

Driver effect (on `jobStream.status` change):
- `"completed"` → resolve `jobStream.result.primary_path` (or `outputs`) into the right `picks` slot for `runningStage`, clear `runningStage`, set `gate` to that stage's review/pick state.
- `"failed"` → set `stageError` for `runningStage`; show inline error + **Retry this stage** button (re-issue the same `runStage` call). Do **not** dead-end the run.

Stage launcher helper:
```js
async function launch(stage, body, nextGate) {
  try {
    setStageError(null);
    const { job_id } = await runStage(stage, body);
    setRunningStage(stage); setJobId(job_id); setGate(nextGate);  // nextGate = "<stage>:running"
  } catch (e) {
    setStageError(e instanceof ConflictError
      ? "Another job is already running — wait for it to finish, then retry."
      : e.message);
  }
}
```
Handle `ConflictError` (imported from `api.js`) on every launch — a job from another view may be live (single-job server constraint).

Selection → auto-advance (selecting IS the trigger for the next stage):
- `pickTrend(path)` → `setPicks(trendPath:path)` → `launch("research", { niche: seed, repos: [], mode:"deep", trend_repo: path }, "research:running")`
- `approveResearch()` → `launch("ideation", { topic: seed, research_file: picks.briefPath, no_trends:false }, "ideation:running")`
- `pickIdea(title)` → `launch("hook", { topic: title, platform:"yt-long", audience:"", format:"medium", research_file: picks.briefPath, no_polish:false }, "hook:running")`
- `approveHooks()` → `launch("outline", { topic: picks.ideaTitle, hook_path: picks.hooksPath, length:8, platform:"yt-long", no_polish:false }, "outline:running")`
- `approveOutline()` → `launch("title", { concept: picks.ideaTitle, outline_file: picks.outlinePath }, "title:running")`
- `pickTitle(str)` → `launch("cascade", { research_file: picks.briefPath, outline_file: picks.outlinePath, title: str, youtube_url:"" }, "cascade:running")`
- `approveCascade()` → `launch("short-form", { research_file: picks.briefPath, outline_file: picks.outlinePath, title: picks.titleString, youtube_url:"" }, "shortform:running")`
- short-form `completed` → terminal "done" state.

Rendering — a vertical list of step cards, each in one of: `locked` (not reached), `running` (live log from `jobStream.lines` in a `<pre>` + spinner), `awaiting` (the gate UI below), `done` (collapsed summary of the pick). Reuse existing components:
- **Trends pick:** `VaultPicker` with `folder="04-Trends"` `subfoldersOnly` for the list, a **Refresh trends** button → `launch("trends", { space: seed }, "trends:running")` then re-mount the picker on completion, and a "Use this trend → run Research" confirm.
- **Approve gates (research/hook/outline):** `<MarkdownViewer path={picks.<x>Path} />` + a "Use this → run <next>" button.
- **Ideation pick:** fetch content via `readVaultFile(primary_path)`, parse headings → render selectable cards; clicking a card = `pickIdea(title)`.
- **Title pick:** fetch content, parse `- **title**` lines → selectable list; clicking = `pickTitle(str)`.
- **Cascade / short-form:** `<OutputBrowser result={jobStream.result} />` (handles bundle member tabs).

Parsing (inline helpers in this file — minimal surface, per §2 Simplicity; advisor: parse only what the next stage consumes):
```js
function parseIdeas(md) {
  const out = []; const re = /^#{2,3}\s+Rank\s+\d+\s*[—–-]\s*(.+?)\s*$/gm; let m;
  while ((m = re.exec(md))) out.push(m[1].trim());
  return out;
```
